name: Pumpkin Soup with Goat Cheese & Chickpea-Kale Sauté

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas; set aside to drain further.
Preheat a medium saucepan over medium heat.
While the saucepan heats up, trim off and discard the ends of the onion and remove the outer layer; small dice the onion into 6-mm pieces.
Once the saucepan is hot, add olive oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
instructions.secondary_message: 1 ½ tbsp extra virgin olive oil

instructions.primary_message: Add the onion to the saucepan; cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3 to 4 minutes.
Trim off and discard the root ends of the garlic; peel and mince or press the garlic. Transfer to a small bowl.
Add ½ of the garlic, cinnamon, and crushed red pepper to the saucepan; stir until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
instructions.secondary_message:
¾ tsp cinnamon
⅜ tsp crushed red pepper

instructions.primary_message: Add the pumpkin purée and broth to the saucepan; stir to incorporate and season with salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ (398 ml) can pure pumpkin purée
1775 ml (7 ½ cups) chicken or vegetable broth
1 ½ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Preheat a nonstick skillet over medium heat.
While the skillet heats up, cut out and discard the kale stems; chop the leaves into 2 ½-cm pieces.
Once the pan is hot, add olive oil and swirl to coat the bottom.
Add the remaining garlic and crushed red pepper to the pan; stir until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds.
Add the kale to the skillet and toss with the garlic and olive oil; cook until it is tender, 4 to 6 minutes.
Crumble the goat cheese and place in a small bowl.
Add the chickpeas to the kale and season the mixture with salt and pepper; mix together and continue to cook until the chickpeas are heated through, 1 to 2 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ tsp salt
¾ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Juice the lemons and drizzle over the kale and chickpeas.
Using an immersion (hand) blender, purée the soup until smooth.
To serve, divide the soup between bowls and top with the goat cheese; serve with the sautéed chickpeas and kale on the side. Enjoy!
